context.body: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says the LORD.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

context.body: Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory · Jeremiah 23:1–8
context.label: Canonical location

observations.body: Failed shepherds who scatter are addressed; a remnant is gathered, shepherds appointed, and a righteous Branch for David reigns wisely while Judah and Israel dwell safely.
observations.label: A righteous Branch is raised for David: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps failed shepherds, the remnant, appointed shepherds, David’s Branch, Judah, Israel, and the LORD, scattered lands, pasture, Judah, and Israel, destroying and scattering, gathering, appointing, raising a branch, reigning, executing justice, saving, and dwelling safely visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read Jeremiah 23:1–8 as its own royal, poetic, and prophetic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Davidic rule enters a prophetic answer to failed shepherding inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
